lead: Prelabour rupture of membranes is rupture before contractions start. At term (PROM) it is physiological; before 37 wk (PPROM) it is pathological and causes about 40% of preterm births. The two dangers are infection and prematurity.
f: PROM: at 37 wk or more, 8–10% of term births · PPROM: before 37 wk, about 2% of pregnancies · Prolonged ROM: over 24 h before birth · Causes: infection (BV, GBS, UTI, STIs), previous PPROM, twins, polyhydramnios, cervical weakness, amniocentesis, APH, smoking

Sudden gush, then a slow leak, worse on standing · Sterile speculum: pool in the posterior fornix or leak on coughing (after lying 20–30 min) · Nitrazine turns blue (false positive with blood, semen, BV) · Fern test on a dried slide · Ultrasound: low AFI supports · Differential: urine (acidic), discharge, show; liquor is alkaline (pH 7–7.5)

tr: No digital VE unless she is in labour: each VE carries bacteria up
sc: 32 wk, gush of clear fluid, no pains → Sterile speculum; no digital VE

f: Mother: chorioamnionitis → sepsis, abruption, endometritis · Fetus: prematurity (leading cause of death), sepsis, cord prolapse, lung hypoplasia (ROM before 24 wk)

Admit at least 48–72 h · Erythromycin 250 mg oral 6-hourly × 10 days (or until labour) · Steroids 24–34 wk · MgSO₄ under 32 wk if birth expected within 24 h · No tocolysis (may hide infection) · Temperature, pulse, tenderness 4-hourly; FBC, CRP 2–3 times a week; daily CTG (FHR rising is an early sign) · Deliver at 37 wk if well; at once with infection, fetal distress or abruption

tr: No co-amoxiclav in PPROM: it raises necrotising enterocolitis
sc: PPROM 30 wk, FHR 175, fever → IV antibiotics + deliver

f: About 75% labour within 24 h · Observations and CTG as for PPROM, no steroids · Induce now (oxytocin; prostaglandin if unfavourable) or wait up to 24 h, then induce · Induce at once with meconium, GBS or any sign of infection · GBS prophylaxis if positive, ROM over 24 h or preterm · High head or malpresentation: check the FHR for cord prolapse · CS only for obstetric reasons

sc: Term PROM 26 h, no labour → Induce with oxytocin
Term PROM, GBS positive → IV penicillin, induce now

f: Ascending infection of membranes, liquor and placenta (GBS, E. coli, anaerobes) · Mother: fever over 37.8 °C, tachycardia, uterine tenderness, offensive liquor · Fetal tachycardia over 160, often the first sign · Rising WBC and CRP; HVS and blood cultures · Ampicillin + gentamicin + metronidazole IV, continued after birth · Deliver at any gestation; CS only for obstetric reasons; no tocolysis; never wait for steroids · Complications: sepsis, PPH, endometritis; neonatal sepsis, meningitis, cerebral palsy

tr: Antibiotics alone cannot clear an infected uterus
sc: Chorioamnionitis at 28 wk → IV antibiotics and deliver; do not wait for steroids
